formula_checks.name: isAlternative
formula_checks.why: It decides 'alternative' from the kind list alone and ignores the person's own class answer (MK-XS-I-048) and name evidence, which assetClassOf (MK-NW-F-011) honours first. The two cards describe the same thing differently: a hedge-fund-kind account the person classed as Stocks / Funds passes isAlternative but is not Alternatives by assetClassOf; a 'stocks'-kind fund the person classed as Alternatives fails isAlternative but is Alternatives by assetClassOf. Wherever both are used for one screen (theAlternativesOutlook), the rows stop adding to the total.
formula_checks.should_be: isAlternative(a) = (assetClassOf(a) is Alternatives). One definition, one function (owner DEC-0343).
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0343 (one concept, one function); assetClassOf step (1) honouring the stated class; MK-NW-M-049 must equal the Net worth tab's Alternatives slice.

formula_checks.name: valueFreshness
formula_checks.why: 'Whole calendar months from the value date's month to this month' counts month boundaries crossed, not months elapsed. A value set on 30 April is called 6 months old — and stale — on 1 October, after 5 months and 1 day; a value set 20 Nov 2025 reads 11 months on 4 Oct 2026 after 10 months and 14 days. The stale line therefore fires up to a month early.
formula_checks.should_be: Months old = completed months between the value date and today: (year difference × 12 + month difference), less 1 when today's day of the month is before the value date's day; never below zero. Stale when that is 6 or more.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary calendar arithmetic; 'a line on the wrong side' check in the brief.

formula_checks.name: portfolioActualReturn
formula_checks.why: The card says it is VALUE-weighted, but the formula weights each account by the amount EARMARKED for retirement and drops any account with no earmark. A $95,000 brokerage earmarked 0% for retirement disappears from 'your portfolio's actual return'; a taxable account earmarked 25% counts at a quarter of its size. The earmark is a goal split, not a holding size, and has no bearing on what the money earned. Also: a reported return of 0 must count (only a missing one is left out), and under the owner's 2026-10-04 rule every return is time-weighted, so the reported trailing-12-month figures must be time-weighted returns and the label must say so.
formula_checks.should_be: Over accounts that are not real assets and have a reported trailing-12-month return (zero included, missing excluded): Σ(balance × reported return) ÷ Σ balance. No answer when no account qualifies or the balance total is zero. Each reported figure is a time-weighted return.
formula_checks.rests_on: The card's own 'what_it_is_for' (value-weighted); owner instruction 2026-10-04 (every return is a time-weighted return); standard practice: a composite return weights members by assets.

formula_checks.name: accountAllowsTicker
formula_checks.why: Blocking by class is too blunt for two real accounts: a fixed-income account holding bond ETFs (BND, VGIT — tickered securities) is classed Bonds & CDs and so cannot record them; a brokerage the person classed as Alternatives cannot record the tickered holdings it holds. The card does not say whether 'class' is the stated class or the kind's class.
formula_checks.should_be: Decide by the account's KIND (wrapper and institution type): false for checking, savings and other bank cash accounts, 529 plans, CDs and property; true for brokerage, retirement wrappers, HSA and fixed-income brokerage accounts — not by the asset class the person or a name assigned.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary practice: bond ETFs and funds trade by ticker; owner DEC-0092 files bond funds and money-market funds by what they are, not by account.

formula_checks.name: assetKind
formula_checks.why: A lookup by id that returns nothing for an id not in the list is the honest answer. The card is silent on case and spaces ('Checking', ' 401k '); ids come from the app's own list, so exact matching is defensible, but see the RULE UNCLEAR case.

formula_checks.name: maturityClass
formula_checks.why: Matches the founder rule of 2026-08-04 quoted on the card: any maturity-dated instrument is a bond, however soon it matures. Note it conflicts with assetClassOf (MK-NW-F-011), which lets name evidence win over a maturity date — judged there.
formula_checks.rests_on: Founder rule 2026-08-04 (on the card); owner DEC-0051 (CDs/T-bills → Bonds & CDs, any maturity).

formula_checks.name: wrapperAccount
formula_checks.why: For Traditional IRA and HSA the formula gives the tax bucket but no kind, so the account's kind is unstated (and the kind drives contribution limits and later rules). HSA is put in PRE_TAX with no note that qualified medical withdrawals are tax-free, so later projections may tax money that is not taxed. 'Roth' always becomes a Roth IRA, so a Roth 401(k) cannot be expressed.
formula_checks.should_be: Traditional IRA → kind Traditional IRA, PRE_TAX. HSA → kind HSA, PRE_TAX on the way in, with its tax-free medical withdrawals recorded on the kind. Roth → Roth IRA unless a Roth 401(k) is chosen. Anything else or nothing → brokerage, TAXABLE.
formula_checks.rests_on: IRS Publication 969 (2025) — HSA distributions for qualified medical expenses are tax-free; IRS Publication 590-A/B (2025) for IRAs.

formula_checks.name: assetClassOf
formula_checks.why: (1) Step 2 (name evidence) comes before step 3 (maturity date), so a CD named, say, 'Savings Builder CD' is filed as cash on the word 'savings', against the founder rule on MK-NW-F-009 that ANY maturity-dated instrument is a bond — two cards describing the same thing differently. (2) Step 7 files anything that is property and not a home or vehicle as Real estate, so valuables, jewellery, art or a boat entered as property land in Real estate, though the Personal property band is defined as 'vehicles and valuables' (MK-NW-M-006) and the author notes 'a house is not a vehicle, and mixing them hides both'.
formula_checks.should_be: (1) stated class; (2) Bonds & CDs if it has a maturity date; (3) name evidence; (4) kind; (5) Stocks / Funds if it lists holdings; (6) Cash if a cash account; (7) property → Real estate only for home/rental/land kinds (or re_use set); any other property → Personal property; (8) Unclassified.
formula_checks.rests_on: Founder rule 2026-08-04 recorded on MK-NW-F-009; owner DEC-0051; figure MK-NW-M-006 (Personal property = vehicles and valuables).

formula_checks.name: taxTreatmentOf
formula_checks.why: Correct for IRAs, 401(k)s, Roths and taxable accounts. Silent on two wrappers a 55–70 household often holds: a 529 (bucket not pre-tax or Roth) falls to 'taxable', though qualified education withdrawals are tax-free; an HSA falls to 'tax-deferred', though qualified medical withdrawals are tax-free.
formula_checks.should_be: Stated treatment first; then 529 → tax-free (qualified use); HSA → tax-free for medical use (tax-deferred otherwise, stated as such); pre-tax → tax-deferred; Roth → tax-free; otherwise taxable.
formula_checks.rests_on: IRS Publication 970 (2025) for 529 plans; IRS Publication 969 (2025) for HSAs.

formula_checks.name: cashTotal
formula_checks.why: It finds uninvested cash inside an investment account only when the account is linked. A hand-built brokerage that records its own cash sleeve (cash_balance, with derive_balance on) contributes nothing, though the card says the total includes 'the uninvested cash sitting inside investment accounts' and the type says such an account's value is cash_balance + holdings.
formula_checks.should_be: Σ over accounts of: for a linked account, its breakdown's cash slice; for a hand-built account with a recorded cash sleeve, that cash_balance; for any other account, its whole balance when its class is cash; otherwise 0.
formula_checks.rests_on: The card's own 'what_it_is_for'; AssetAccount type comments on cash_balance and derive_balance.

formula_checks.name: investmentsTotal
formula_checks.why: It counts every investment-class account WHOLE, while cashTotal (MK-NW-F-016) takes the cash sleeve out of the same linked accounts — the uninvested cash is counted twice. The approved drawing (networth 01, state A) shows Investments $354,314, without Vanguard's $838 cash; this formula gives $355,152. The reverse also happens: a linked cash-class account holding a CD has its CD counted in neither total.
formula_checks.should_be: Σ over accounts of: for a linked account, the sum of its non-cash slices (Stocks/Funds, Bonds & CDs, Alternatives, Unclassified); for a hand-built account with a cash sleeve, balance − cash_balance; for any other account, its whole balance when its class is an investment class. Invariant: cashTotal + investmentsTotal = investableAssets.
formula_checks.rests_on: Approved drawing 'Net worth, Quiet Instrument v08, state A'; owner DEC-0343 (a total and the sum of its parts pinned by an invariant).

formula_checks.name: investableAssets
formula_checks.why: Everything not a real asset, counted whole — no double counting, because each account is counted once. It is the figure cashTotal and investmentsTotal must add up to.

formula_checks.name: accountDisplayNames
formula_checks.why: Two cases change the names shown. (1) 'In order of account id' does not say whether ids sort as text or as numbers; ids '9' and '10' swap their · 1 / · 2 between the two readings. (2) A suffixed name can collide with an account already named that way: two 'Savings' and one 'Savings · 1' produce two accounts both shown as 'Savings · 1' — the duplication the function exists to remove.
formula_checks.should_be: Name the id order (text order, or creation order). After adding suffixes, check the whole list again and skip any suffix already taken, so every display name is unique.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic; the card's own purpose.

formula_checks.name: accountClassBreakdown
formula_checks.why: (1) A holding with no price is valued at 0; when its true value is within the tolerance (max $1, 1% of balance) the gap it leaves is added to CASH. An unpriced $1,500 stock in a $195,000 account becomes $1,500 of cash — and cash feeds the emergency fund. (2) 'Value = shares × last price' is silent on the option multiplier: 3 contracts at $8.45 are $2,535, not $25.35; under the literal reading the gap exceeds tolerance and the option's value is filed under the account's own class instead of Alternatives. (3) The card's 'what_it_is_for' still says money market goes under cash; owner DEC-0051/0092/0309 put money-market funds under Stocks / Funds.
formula_checks.should_be: Unpriced holdings are not zero: the gap is filed under the unpriced holdings' own class (or an 'unpriced' line) before any rounding plug; only a gap with no unpriced holding left is a rounding remainder that may go to cash. Option value = contracts × price × 100 (or the stated multiplier). Money-market funds → Stocks / Funds.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0051, DEC-0092, DEC-0309; standard equity option contract size, 100 shares (OCC); author rule r30 elsewhere ('a holding priced at zero would quietly shrink your portfolio').

formula_checks.name: classPortionLabel
formula_checks.why: Right in shape (owner DEC-0090: '3 CD & 1 treasury bond in this account'). Silent on: one item ('1 holdings'); a zero count ('0 options & 2 holdings'); how a name 'says CD' — a plain substring test reads 'ABCD Industries 5.1% 2031' as a CD; whether capitals matter ('ally cd'); and what is listed when there are CDs, Treasuries AND other bonds.
formula_checks.should_be: Count CDs and Treasuries by whole-word match, capitals ignored; singular for one ('1 CD', '1 holding'); leave out any part whose count is zero; join three parts as 'A, B & C in this account'.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner DEC-0090; owner DEC-0406 (always be explicit).
